previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 58-year-old woman with type 1 diabetes, bilateral below-knee amputations, and a history of recurrent multidrug-resistant urinary tract infections was admitted for hyperkalemia and acute kidney injury. She had recently completed a course of colistin, which was suspected to cause nephrotoxicity. Her potassium was elevated at 5.5 on presentation and managed with insulin and kayexalate in the emergency department. Creatinine peaked at 4.7 and stabilized at 4.4 with IV fluids. Renal ultrasound showed no hydronephrosis, supporting intrinsic kidney injury. The patient remained asymptomatic, with no signs of active infection; urine culture showed no growth. She was discharged home with instructions to follow up with nephrology, urology, and her primary care provider, advised to continue a low-potassium, low-phosphate diet, and to stop oral vancomycin. Medications were adjusted for renal function, and lisinopril was held.

PICC LINE PLACEMENT

INDICATION:  IV access needed for antibiotics.

The procedure was explained to the patient.  A timeout was performed.

RADIOLOGISTS:  Dr. ___ and Dr. ___.

TECHNIQUE:  Using sterile technique and local anesthesia, the right basilic
vein was punctured under direct ultrasound guidance using a micropuncture set.
Hard copies of ultrasound images were obtained before and immediately after
establishing intravenous access are on file.  A peel-away sheath was then
placed over a guidewire and a PowerPICC line measuring 35 cm in length was
then placed through the peel-away sheath with its tip positioned in the SVC
under fluoroscopic guidance.  Position of the catheter was confirmed by a
fluoroscopic spot film of the chest.

The peel-away sheath and guidewire were then removed.  The catheter was
secured to the skin, flushed, and a sterile dressing applied.

The patient tolerated the procedure well.  There were no immediate
complications.

IMPRESSION:  Uncomplicated ultrasound and fluoroscopically guided single lumen
PICC line placement via the right basilic venous approach.  Final internal
length is 35 cm, with the tip positioned in SVC.  The line is ready to use.

The uterus is normal.  Within the right ovary, there is a 4-mm calcification

There is edema and enhancement within the hamstring muscles bilaterally,

There is also moderate edema and enhancement surrounding the hip joints

Small lymph nodes within the bilateral external iliac chains, the largest
measuring 9 mm in the left external iliac chain (12:21).  Multiple small
